title: Identification of genetic variations in patients with aortic type B dissection
summary:
Background: Aortic dissection is a life threatening disease. The pathophysiology is mostly uncertain, however more and more studies reveal genetical mutations and variations that may impact connective tissue integrity.
In this study we are planning to register all patients that present with acute aortic type B dissection. Familial anamnesis and a clinical examination are performed to identify familial or phenotypical abnormalities. Blood samples are taken to identify genetic risk variants that influence connective tissue components. Other genetic findings are not investigated or conveyed to the patient. Skin biopsies are taken in selected patients with suspicion for connective tissue disease from the upper arm. Electron microscopy is performed to detect elastic fiber alteration.
If open surgical procedures are considered, vessel wall biopsies could be taken for vascular biobanking. Aim of this study is to detect novel genetic risk variants for aortic dissection and a patient specific follow-up care.

interventions.name: Registration of patients with aortic type B dissection, connective tissue gene investigation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included will be patients over 18 years that are reffered to the department of vascular and endovascular surgery (University Hospital Heidelberg). Aortic type B dissection will be diagnosed with Computer tomography angiography (CT-A) or magnetic resonance angiography (MR-A) independetly to the study protocol. Both complicated, uncomplicated acute and chronic type B dissections will be included into the study. 
Patients give their written consent for genetic analysis and skin biopsy.
Exclusion criteria:
pregnant women, age < 18, traumatic aortic dissection, refusal of patient consent, local anesthetic intolerance (no skin biopsy!)
